name: Asclepiades of Samos
bio: Asclepiades of Samos was a Hellenistic epigrammatist of the early third century BC. He is counted among the poets who shaped the short Greek love poem, and Meleager's Garland drew heavily on his work.
The poems collected here are the epigrams that Paton's first volume ascribes to him, chiefly in Book V.

poems.title: Book V, 7
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text: Dear lamp, thrice Heraclea here present swore by thee to come and cometh not. Lamp, if thou art a god, take vengeance on the deceitful girlk When she has a friend at home and is sporting with him, go out, and give them no more light.

poems.title: Book V, 64
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text: Snow, hail, make darkness, lighten, thunder, shake out upon the earth all thy black clouds! If thou slayest me, then I shall cease, but if thou lettest me live, though I pass through worse than this, I will. go with music to her doors; for the god compels me who is thy master too, Zeus, he at whose bidding thou, turned to gold, didst pierce the brazen chamber.

poems.title: Book V, 85
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text: Thou grudgest thy maidenhead? What avails it? When thou goest to Hades thou shalt find none to love thee there. The joys of Love are in the land of the living, but in Acheron, dear virgin, we shall lie dust and ashes.

poems.title: Book V, 145
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text: Answer here, my garlands, where I hang ye by this door, nor shake off your leaves in haste, for I have watered you with my tears—rainy are the eyes of lovers. But when the door opens and ye see him, shed my rain on his head, that at least his fair hair may drink my tears.

poems.title: Book V, 150
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text: The celebrated Nico promised to come to me for to-night and swore by solemn Demeter. She comes not and the first watch of night is past. Did she mean then to forswear herself? Servants, put out the light.

poems.title: Book V, 153
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text: Nicarere’s sweet face, bathed by the Loves, peeping often from her high casement, was blasted, dear Cypris, by the flame that lightened from the sweet blue eyes of Cleophon, standing by her door,

poems.title: Book V, 158
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text: I played once with captivating Hermione, and she wore, O Paphian Queen, a zone of many colours bearing letters of gold; all round it was written, “Love me and be not sore at heart if I am another’s.”

poems.title: Book V, 162
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text: Cruel Philaenion has bitten me; though the bite does not show, the pain reaches to my finger-tips. Dear Loves, I am gone, ‘tis over with me, I am past hope; for half-asleep I trod upon a whore, I know it, and her touch was death.

poems.title: Book V, 164
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text: Night, for I call thee alone to witness, look how shamefully Nico’s Pythias, ever loving to deceive, treats me. I came at her call and not uninvited. May she one day stand at my door and complain to thee that she suffered the like at my hands.

poems.title: Book V, 167
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text: It was night, it was raining, and, love’s third burden, I was in wine; the north wind blew cold and I was alone. But lovely Moschus overpowered all. “Would thou didst wander so, and didst not rest at one door.’ So much I exclaimed there, drenched through. “How long Zeus? Peace, dear Zeus! Thou too didst learn to love.”

poems.title: Book V, 169
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text: Sweet in summer a draught of snow to him who thirsts, and sweet for sailors after winter’s storms to feel the Zephyr of the spring. But sweeter still when one cloak doth cover two lovers and Cypris hath honour from both

poems.title: Book V, 181
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text: Buy us some . . . (but when will he come ?) and five rose wreaths.—Why do you say “pax”’!? You say you have no change! We are ruined; won't someone string up the Lapith beast! I have a brigand not a servant. So you are not at fault! Not at all! Bring your account. Phryne, fetch me my reckoning counters. Oh the rascal! Wine, five drachmae! Sausage, two! ormers you say, mackerel . ... honeycombs! We will reckon them up correctly to-morrow; now go to Aeschra’s perfumery and get five silver bottles (?) Tell her as a token that Bacchon kissed her five times right off, of which fact her bed was entered as a witness.

poems.title: Book V, 185
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text: Go to the market, Demetrius, and get from Amyntas three small herrings and ten little lemon-soles!; and get two dozen fresh prawns (he will count them for you) and come straight back. And from Thauborius get six rose-wreaths—and, as it is on your way, just look in and invite Tryphera.

poems.title: Book V, 189
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text: The night is long, and it is winter weather, and night sets when the Pleiads are half-way up the sky. I pass and repass her door, drenched by the rain, smitten by desire of her, the deceiver. It is not love that Cypris smote me with, but a tormenting arrow red-hot from the fire.

poems.title: Book V, 203
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text: Lysidice dedicated to thee, Cypris, her spur, the golden goad of her shapely leg, with which she trained many a horse on its back, while her own thighs were never reddened, so lightly did she ride ; for she ever finished the race without a touch of the spur, and therefore hung on the great gate of thy temple this her weapon of gold.

poems.title: Book V, 207
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text: Bitto and Nannion of Samus will not go to the house of Cypris by the road the goddess ordains, but desert to other things which are not seemly. O Lady Cypris, look with hate on the truants from thy bed.

poems.title: Book V, 210
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text: Didyme by the branch she waved at me has carried me clean away, alas! and looking on her beauty, I melt like wax before the fire. And if she is dusky, what is that to me? So are the coals, but when we light them, they shine as bright as roses.

poems.title: Book VI, 308
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text: Connarus, on winning the boys’ contest, since he wrote such a pretty hand, received eighty knucklebones, and in gratitude to the Muses he hung me up here, the comic mask of old Chares, amid the applause of the boys.

poems.title: Book VII, 11: On Erinna (inscribed on a Volume of her Poems)
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text: This is the sweet work of Erinna, not great indeed in volume, as being that of a maiden of nineteen, but greater in power than that of many others. If Death had not come early to me, who would have had such a name?

poems.title: Book VII, 145: On Ajax
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text: Here sit I, miserable Virtue, by this tomb of Ajax, with shorn hair, smitten with heavy sorrow that cunning Fraud hath more power with the Greeks than I,

poems.title: Book VII, 217: A slightly different version is attributed by Athenaeus to Plato
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text: I hold Archeanassa the courtesan from Colophon even on whose wrinkles sweet Love sat. Ah, ye lovers, who plucked the fresh flowers of her youth in its first piercing brilliance, through what a fiery furnace did you pass!

poems.title: Book VII, 284
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text: Keep off from me, thou fierce sea, eight cubits’ space and swell and roar with all thy might. But if thou dost destroy the tomb of Eumares, naught shall it profit thee, for naught shalt thou find but bones and ashes.

poems.title: Book VII, 500
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text: Wayfarer who passest by my empty tomb, when thou comest to Chios tell my father Melesagoras that the evil south-easter destroyed me, my ship, and my merchandise, and naught but the name of Euippus is left.:

poems.title: Book IX, 63
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text: Lyde is my name and I am of Lydian race, and Antimachus has made me more noble than any descendant of Codrus.?, For who has not sung me, who has not read Lyde, the joint work of the Muses and Antimachus ?

poems.title: Book IX, 64
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text: The Muses themselves saw thee, Hesiod, feeding thy sheep at mid-day in the rugged hills, and all drawing round thee proffered thee a branch of holy laurel with lovely leaves. They gave thee also the inspiring water of the Heliconian spring, that the hoof of the winged horse once struck, and having drunk thy fill of it thou didst write in verse the Birth of the gods and the Works, and the race of the ancient demigods.

poems.title: Book IX, 752
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.note: Also attributed to Antipater of Thessalonica.
poems.text: I am Drunkenness, the work of a skilled hand, but I am carved on the sober stone amethyst. The stone is foreign to the work. But I am the sacred possession of Cleopatra: on the queen’s hand even the drunken goddess should be sober.

poems.title: Book XII, 46
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text: I am not yet two and twenty, and life is a burden to me. Ye Loves, why thus maltreat me; why set me afire? For if I perish, what will you do? Clearly, Loves, you will play, silly children, at your knuckle-bones as before.

poems.title: Book XII, 50
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text: Drink, Asclepiades. Why these tears? What aileth thee? Not thee alone hath cruel Cypris taken captive; not for thee alone hath bitter Love sharpened his arrows. Why whilst yet alive dost thou lie in the dust? Let us quaff the unmixed drink of Bacchus. The day is but a finger’s breadth. Shall we wait to see again the lamp that bids us to bed? Let us drink, woeful lover. It is not far away now, poor wretch, the time when we shall rest through the long night.

poems.title: Book XII, 75
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text: If thou hadst wings on thy back, and a bow and arrows in thy hand, not Love but thou wouldst be described as the son of Cypris.

poems.title: Book XII, 105
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text: I am a little love that flew away, still easy to catch, from my mother’s nest, but from the house of Damis I fly not away on high; but here, loving and beloved without a rival, I keep company not with many, but with one in happy union.

poems.title: Book XII, 135
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text: Wine is the proof of love. Nicagoras denied to us that he was in love, but those many toasts convicted him. Yes he shed tears and bent his head, and had a certain downcast look, and the wreath bound tight round his head kept not its place.

poems.title: Book XII, 153
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.note: Paton’s heading: “(The Complaint of a Girl)”.
poems.text: Time was when Archeades loved to sit close to me, but now not even in play does he turn to look at me, unhappy that I am. Not even Love the honeyed is ever sweet, but often he becomes a sweeter god to lovers when he torments them.

poems.title: Book XII, 161
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text: Dorcion, who loves to sport with the young men, knows how to cast, like a tender boy, the swift dart of Cypris the Popular, flashing desire from her eye, and over her shoulders . . . with her boy’s hat, her chlamys showed her naked thigh.

poems.title: Book XII, 162
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text: My Love, not yet carrying a bow, or savage, but a tiny child, returns to Cypris, holding a golden writing tablet, and reading from it he lisps the love-charms that Diaulus’ boy, Philocrates, used to conquer the soul of Antigenes.

poems.title: Book XII, 163
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text: Love has discovered what beauty to mix with beauty ; not emerald with gold, which neither sparkles nor could ever be its equal, nor ivory with ebony, black with white, but Cleander with Eubiotus, two flowers of Persuasion and Friendship.

poems.title: Book XII, 166
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text: Let this that is left of my soul, whatever it be, let this at least, ye Loves, have rest for heaven’s sake. Or else no longer shoot me with arrows but with thunderbolts, and make me utterly into ashes and cinders. Yea yea strike me, ye Loves; for withered away as I am by distress, I would have from you, if I may have aught, this little gift.

poems.title: Book XIII, 23
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.note: Paton’s metre label: ‘Tetrameters, composed of complete trimeters with the addition of a final basis, followed by imperfect trimeters’.
poems.text: Ho passer by; even if thou art in haste give ear a moment to the grief of Botrys that passeth measure. An old man now of four-score years, he buried his boy of nine, a child already speaking with some skill and wisdom. Alas for thy father and alas for thee, dear son of Botrys; with how many joys untasted hast thou perished!

poems.title: Book XVI, 68
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text: This is a statue of Cypris. But come let us see if it be not Berenice’s. I am in doubt of which one should say it is the better likeness.

poems.title: Laus Veneris (Mackail)
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Sweet is snow in summer for the thirsty to drink, and sweet for sailors after winter to see the garland of spring; but most sweet when one cloak shelters two lovers, and the tale of love is told by both.

poems.title: Love in the Storm (Mackail)
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Snow, hail, darken, blaze, thunder, shake forth all thy glooming clouds upon the earth; for if thou slay me, then will I cease, but while thou lettest me live, though thou handle me worse than this, I will revel. For the god draws me who is thy master too, at whose persuasion, Zeus, thou didst once pierce in gold to that brazen bridal-chamber.

poems.title: Waiting in Vain (Mackail)
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Nico the renowned consented to come to me at nightfall and swore by the holy Lady of Laws; and she is not come, and the watch is gone by; did she mean to forswear herself? Servants, put out the lamp.

poems.title: The Scorned Lover (Mackail)
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: O Night, thee and none other I take to witness, how Nico's Pythias flouts me, traitress as she is; asked, not unasked am I come; may she yet blame thee in the selfsame plight standing by my doors!

poems.title: The Burden of Youth (Mackail)
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: I am not two and twenty yet, and I am weary of living; O Loves, why misuse me so? why set me on fire; for when I am gone, what will you do? Doubtless, O Loves, as before you will play with your dice, unheeding.

poems.title: The Dew of Tears (Mackail)
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Stay there, my garlands, hanging by these doors, nor hastily scattering your petals, you whom I have wetted with tears (for lovers' eyes are rainy); but when you see him as the door opens, drip my rain over his head, that so at least that golden hair may drink my tears.

poems.title: Dust and Ashes (Mackail)
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Thou hoardest thy maidenhood; and to what profit? for when thou art gone to Hades thou wilt not find a lover, O girl. Among the living are the Cyprian's pleasures; but in Acheron, O maiden, we shall lie bones and dust.

poems.title: Who So Pale and Wan, Fond Lover (Mackail)
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Drink, Asclepiades; why these tears? what ails thee? not of thee only has the cruel Cyprian made her prey, nor for thee only bitter Love whetted the arrows of his bow; why while yet alive liest thou in the dust?

poems.title: A Grave by the Sea (Mackail)
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Keep eight cubits away from me, O rough sea, and billow and roar with all thy might; but if thou pullest down the grave of Eumares, thou wilt find nothing of value, but only bones and dust.

poems.title: Fleeting Dawn (Mackail)
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Let us drink an unmixed draught of wine; dawn is an hand-breadth; are we waiting to see the bed-time lamp once again? Let us drink merrily; after no long time yet, O luckless one, we shall sleep through the long night.

poems.title: The Praise of Love
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text:
Sweet is the snow in summer thirst to drink, and sweet the day
When sailors see spring's garland bloom and winter pass away.
But the sweetest thing on earth is when, one mantle for their cover,
Two hearts recite the Cyprian's praise as lover unto lover.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca V.7: λύχνε, σὲ γὰρ παρεοῦσα τρὶς
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text:
λύχνε, σὲ γὰρ παρεοῦσα τρὶς ὤμοσεν Ἡράκλεια
ἥξειν, κοὐχ ἥκει· λύχνε, σὺ δʼ, εἰ θεὸς εἶ,
τὴν δολίην ἀπάμυνον ὅταν φίλον ἔνδον ἔχουσα
παίζῃ, ἀποσβεσθεὶς μηκέτι φῶς πάρεχε.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca V.64: Νῖφε, χαλαζοβόλει, ποίει σκότος, αἶθε
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text:
Νῖφε, χαλαζοβόλει, ποίει σκότος, αἶθε, κεραύνου,
πάντα τὰ πορφύροντʼ ἐν χθονὶ σεῖε νέφη.
ἢν γάρ με κτείνῃς, τότε παύσομαι· ἢν δὲ μʼ ἀφῇς ζῆν,
καὶ διαδὺς τούτων χείρονα, κωμάσομαι
ἕλκει γάρ μʼ ὁ κρατῶν καὶ σοῦ θεός, ᾧ ποτε πεισθείς,
Ζεῦ, διὰ χαλκείων χρυσὸς ἔδυς θαλάμων.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca V.85: φείδῃ παρθενίης· καὶ τί πλέον
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text:
φείδῃ παρθενίης· καὶ τί πλέον; οὐ γὰρ ἐς ᾍδην
ἐλθοῦσ’ εὑρήσεις τὸν φιλέοντα, κόρη.
ἐν ζωοῖσι τὰ τερπνὰ τὰ Κύπριδος; ἐν δʼ Ἀχέροντι
ὀστέα καὶ σποδιή, παρθένε, κεισόμεθα.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca V.153: Νικαρέτης τὸ πόθοισι βεβαμμένον ἡδὺ
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text:
Νικαρέτης τὸ πόθοισι βεβαμμένον ἡδὺ πρόσωπον,
πυκνὰ διʼ ὑψορόφων φαινόμενον θυρίδων,
αἱ χαροπαὶ Κλεοφῶντος ἐπὶ προθύροις ἐμάραναν,
Κύπρι φίλη, γλυκεροῦ βλέμματος ἀστεροπαί.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca V.158: Ἑρμιόνῃ πιθανᾖ ποτʼ ἐγὼ συνέπαιζον
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text:
Ἑρμιόνῃ πιθανᾖ ποτʼ ἐγὼ συνέπαιζον, ἐχούσῃ
ζωνίον ἐξ ἀνθέων ποικίλον, ὦ Παφίη,
χρύσεα γράμματʼ ἔχον διόλου δʼ ἐγέγραπτο, “ φίλει με·
καὶ μὴ λυπηθῇς, ἤν τις ἔχῃ μʼ ἕτερος.”

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca V.162: ἡ λαμυρὴ μʼ ἔτρωσε Φιλαίνιον
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text:
ἡ λαμυρὴ μʼ ἔτρωσε Φιλαίνιον εἰ δὲ τὸ τραῦμα
μὴ σαφές, ἀλλʼ ὁ πόνος δύεται εἰς ὄνυχα.
οἴχομʼ, Ἔρωτες, ὄλωλα, διοίχομαι· εἰς γὰρ ἑταίραν
νυστάζων ἐπέβην, οἶδʼ, ἔθιγον τʼ Ἀίδα.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca V.164: νύξ· σὲ γὰρ οὐκ ἄλλην
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text:
νύξ· σὲ γὰρ οὐκ ἄλλην μαρτύρομαι, οἷά μʼ ὑβρίζει
Πυθιὰς ἡ Νικοῦς, οὖσα φιλεξαπάτις·
κληθείς, οὐκ ἄκλητος, ἐλήλυθα. ταὐτὰ παθοῦσα
σοὶ μέμψαιτʼ ἔτʼ ἐμοῖς στᾶσα παρὰ προθύροις,

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca V.167: ὑετὸς ἦν καὶ νύξ, καὶ
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text:
ὑετὸς ἦν καὶ νύξ, καὶ τὸ τρίτον ἄλγος ἔρωτι,
οἶνος· καὶ Βορέης ψυχρός, ἐγὼ δὲ μόνος.
ἀλλʼ ὁ καλὸς Μόσχος πλέον ἴσχυεν. “αἰ σὺ γὰρ οὕτως
ἤλυες, οὐδὲ θύρην πρὸς μίαν ἡσύχασας.”
τῇδε τοσαῦτʼ ἐβόησα βεβρεγμένος· “ἄχρι τίνος, Ζεῦ;
Ζεῦ φίλε, σίγησον καὐτὸς ἐρᾶν ἔμαθες.”

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca V.169: ἡδὺ θέρους διψῶντι χιὼν ποτόν
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text:
ἡδὺ θέρους διψῶντι χιὼν ποτόν ἡδὺ δὲ ναύταις
ἐκ χειμῶνος ἰδεῖν εἰαρινὸν ζέφυρον·
ἥδιον δʼ ὁπόταν κρύψῃ μία τοὺς φιλέοντας
χλαῖνα, καὶ αἰνῆται Κύπρις ὑπʼ ἀμφοτέρων.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca V.189: νὺξ μακρὴ καὶ χεῖμα, μέσην
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text:
νὺξ μακρὴ καὶ χεῖμα, μέσην δʼ ἐπὶ Πλειάδα δύνει·
κἀγὼ πὰρ προθύροις νίσσομαι ὑόμενος,
τρωθεὶς τῆς δολίης κείνης πόθῳ· οὐ γὰρ ἔρωτα
Κύπρις, ἀνιηρὸν δʼ ἐκ πυρὸς ἧκε βέλος.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca V.203: Λυσιδίκη σοί, Κύπρι, τὸν ἱππαστῆρα
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text:
Λυσιδίκη σοί, Κύπρι, τὸν ἱππαστῆρα μύωπα,
χρύσεον εὐκνήμου κέντρον ἔθηκε ποδός,
ᾧ πολὺν ὕπτιον ἵππον ἐγύμνασεν οὐ δὲ ποτʼ αὐτῆς
μηρὸς ἐφοινίχθη κοῦφα τινασσομένης·
ἦν γὰρ ἀκέντητος τελεοδρόμος· οὕνεκεν ὅπλον
σοὶ κατὰ μεσσοπύλης χρύσεον ἐκρέμασεν.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca V.207: αἱ Σάμιαι Βιττὼ καὶ Νάννιον
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text:
αἱ Σάμιαι Βιττὼ καὶ Νάννιον εἰς Ἀφροδίτης
φοιτᾶν τοῖς αὐτῆς οὐκ ἐθέλουσι νόμοις,
εἰς δʼ ἕτερʼ αὐτομολοῦσιν, ἃ μὴ καλά. δεσπότι Κύπρι,
μίσει τὰς κοίτης τῆς παρὰ σοὶ φυγάδας,

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca V.210: τῷ θαλλῷ Διδύμη με συνήρπασεν
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text:
τῷ θαλλῷ Διδύμη με συνήρπασεν ὤ μοι. ἐγὼ δὲ
τήκομαι, ὡς κηρὸς πὰρ πυρί, κάλλος ὁρῶν.
εἰ δὲ μέλαινα, τί τοῦτο; καὶ ἄνθρακες· ἀλλʼ ὅτʼ ἐκείνους
θάλψωμεν, λάμπουσ’ ὡς ῥόδεαι κάλυκες.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.308: νικήσας τοὺς παῖδας, ἐπεὶ καλὰ
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text:
νικήσας τοὺς παῖδας, ἐπεὶ καλὰ γράμματʼ ἔγραψεν,
Κόνναρος ὀγδώκοντʼ ἀστραγάλους ἔλαβεν,
κἀμέ, χάριν Μούσαις, τὸν κωμικὸν ὧδε Χάρητα
πρεσβύτην θορύβῳ θήκατο παιδαρίων.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.11: Ὁ γλυκὺς Ἠρίννης οὗτος πόνος
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text:
Ὁ γλυκὺς Ἠρίννης οὗτος πόνος, οὐχὶ πολὺς μέν,
ὡς ἂν παρθενικᾶς ἐννεακαιδεκέτευς,
ἀλλʼ ἑτέρων πολλῶν δυνατώτερος· εἰ δʼ Ἀίδας μοι
μὴ ταχὺς ἦλθε, τίς ἂν ταλίκον ἔσχʼ ὄνομα;

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.145: ἅδʼ ἐγὼ ἁ τλάμων Ἀρετὰ
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text:
ἅδʼ ἐγὼ ἁ τλάμων Ἀρετὰ παρὰ τῷδε κάθημαι
Αἴαντος τύμβῳ κειραμένα πλοκάμους,
θυμὸν ἄχει μεγάλῳ βεβολημένα, εἰ παρʼ Ἀχαιοῖς
ἁ δολόφρων Ἀπάτα κρέσσον ἐμεῦ δύναται.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.217: Ἀρχεάνασσαν ἔχω, τὰν ἐκ Κολοφῶνος
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text:
Ἀρχεάνασσαν ἔχω, τὰν ἐκ Κολοφῶνος ἑταίραν,
ἇς καὶ ἐπὶ ῥυτίδων ὁ γλυκὺς ἕζετʼ Ἔρως.
ἆ νέον ἥβης ἄνθος ἀποδρέψαντες ἐρασταὶ
πρωτοβόλου, διʼ ὅσης ἤλθετε πυρκαϊῆς.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.284: ὀκτώ μευ πήχεις ἄπεχε, τρηχεῖα
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text:
ὀκτώ μευ πήχεις ἄπεχε, τρηχεῖα θάλασσα,
καὶ κύμαινε, βόα θʼ ἡλίκα σοι δύναμις·
ἢν δὲ τὸν Εὐμάρεω καθέλῃς τάφον, ἄλλο μὲν οὐδὲν
κρήγυον, εὑρήσεις δʼ ὀστέα καὶ σποδιήν.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.500: ὦ παρʼ ἐμὸν στείχων κενὸν
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text:
ὦ παρʼ ἐμὸν στείχων κενὸν ἠρίον, εἶπον, ὁδῖτα,
εἰς Χίον εὖτʼ ἂν ἵκῃ, πατρὶ Μελησαγόρῃ,
ὡς ἐμὲ μὲν καὶ νῆα καὶ ἐμπορίην κακὸς Εὖρος
ὤλεσεν, Εὐίππου δʼ αὐτὸ λέλειπτʼ ὄνομα.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.63: Λυδὴ καὶ γένος εἰμὶ καὶ
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text:
Λυδὴ καὶ γένος εἰμὶ καὶ οὔνομα· τῶν δʼ ἀπὸ Κόδρου
σεμνοτέρη πασῶν εἰμι διʼ Ἀντίμαχον.
τίς γὰρ ἔμʼ οὐκ ἤεισε; τίς οὐκ ἀνελέξατο Λύδην,
τὸ ξυνὸν Μουσῶν γράμμα καὶ Ἀντιμάχου;

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.64: αὐταὶ ποιμαίνοντα μεσημβρινὰ μῆλά σε
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text:
αὐταὶ ποιμαίνοντα μεσημβρινὰ μῆλά σε Μοῦσαι
ἔδρακον ἐν κραναοῖς οὔρεσιν, Ἡσίοδε,
καί σοι καλλιπέτηλον, ἐρυσσάμεναι περὶ πᾶσαι,
ὤρεξαν δάφνας ἱερὸν ἀκρεμόνα,
δῶκαν δὲ κράνας Ἑλικωνίδος ἔνθεον ὕδωρ,
τὸ πτανοῦ πώλου πρόσθεν ἔκοψεν ὄνυξ·
οὗ σὺ κορεσσάμενος μακάρων γένος ἔργα τε μολπαῖς
καὶ γένος ἀρχαίων ἔγραφες ἡμιθέων.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.752: εἰμὶ Μέθη τὸ γλύμμα σοφῆς
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text:
εἰμὶ Μέθη τὸ γλύμμα σοφῆς χερός, ἐν δʼ ἀμεθύστῳ
γέγλυμμαι· τέχνης δʼ ἡ λίθος ἀλλοτρίη.
ἀλλὰ Κλεοπάτρης ἱερὸν κτέαρ· ἐν γὰρ ἀνάσσης
χειρὶ θεὸν νήφειν καὶ μεθύουσαν ἔδει.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XII.46: οὐκ εἴμʼ οὐδʼ ἐτέων δύο
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text:
οὐκ εἴμʼ οὐδʼ ἐτέων δύο κεἴκοσι, καὶ κοπιῶ ζῶν.
Ὥρωτες, τί κακὸν τοῦτο; τί με φλέγετε;
ἢν γὰρ ἐγώ τι πάθω, τί ποιήσετε; δῆλον, Ἔρωτες,
ὡς τὸ πάρος παίξεσθʼ ἄφρονες ἀστραγάλοις.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XII.50: πῖνʼ, Ἀσκληπιάδη· τί τὰ δάκρυα
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text:
πῖνʼ, Ἀσκληπιάδη· τί τὰ δάκρυα ταῦτα; τί πάσχεις
οὐ σὲ μόνον χαλεπὴ Κύπρις ἐληίσατο,
οὐδʼ ἐπὶ σοὶ μούνῳ κατεθήξατο τόξα καὶ ἰοὺς
πικρὸς Ἔρως. τί ζῶν ἐν σποδιῇ τίθεσαι;
πίνωμεν Βάκχου ζωρὸν πόμα· δάκτυλος ἀώς·
ἦ πάλι κοιμιστὰν λύχνον ἰδεῖν μένομεν;
πίνωμεν, δύσερως· μετά τοι χρόνον οὐκέτι πουλύν,
σχέτλιε, τὴν μακρὰν νύκτʼ ἀναπαυσόμεθα.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XII.75: εἰ πτερά σοι προσέκειτο, καὶ
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text:
εἰ πτερά σοι προσέκειτο, καὶ ἐν χερὶ τόξα καὶ ἰοί,
οὐκ ἂν Ἔρως ἐγράφη Κύπριδος, ἀλλὰ σύ, παῖς.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XII.105: μικρὸς Ἔρως ἐκ μητρὸς ἔτʼ
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text:
μικρὸς Ἔρως ἐκ μητρὸς ἔτʼ εὐθήρατος ἀποπτάς,
ἐξ οἴκων ὑψοῦ Δάμιδος οὐ πέτομαι·
ἀλλʼ αὐτοῦ, φιλέων τε καὶ ἀζήλωτα φιληθείς,
οὐ πολλοῖς, εὐκρὰς δʼ εἷς ἑνὶ συμφέρομαι.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XII.135: οἶνος ἔρωτος ἔλεγχος· ἐρᾶν ἀρνεύμενον
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text:
οἶνος ἔρωτος ἔλεγχος· ἐρᾶν ἀρνεύμενον ἡμῖν
ἤτασαν αἱ πολλαὶ Νικαγόρην προπόσεις.
καὶ γὰρ ἐδάκρυσεν καὶ ἐνύστασε, καί τι κατηφὲς
ἔβλεπε, χὠ σφιγχθεὶς οὐκ ἔμενε στέφανος.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XII.153: πρόσθε μοι Ἀρχεάδης ἐθλίβετο· νῦν
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text:
πρόσθε μοι Ἀρχεάδης ἐθλίβετο· νῦν δὲ τάλαιναν
οὐδʼ ὅσσον παίζων εἰς ἔμʼ ἐπιστρέφεται.
οὐδʼ ὁ μελιχρὸς Ἔρως ἀεὶ γλυκύς· ἀλλʼ ἀνιήσας
πολλάκις ἡδίων γίνετʼ ἐρῶσι θεός.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XII.161: Δόρκιον ἡ φιλέφηβος ἐπίσταται, ὡς
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text:
Δόρκιον ἡ φιλέφηβος ἐπίσταται, ὡς ἁπαλὸς παῖς,
ἕσθαι πανδήμου Κύπριδος ὠκὺ βέλος,
ἵμερον ἀστράπτουσα κατʼ ὄμματος, ἠδʼ ὑπὲρ ὤμων
σὺν πετάσῳ γυμνὸν μηρὸν ἔφαινε χλαμύς.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XII.162: οὔπω τοξοφορῶν οὐδʼ ἄγριος, ἀλλὰ
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text:
οὔπω τοξοφορῶν οὐδʼ ἄγριος, ἀλλὰ νεογνὸς
οὑμὸς Ἔρως παρὰ τὴν Κύπριν ὑποστρέφεται,
δέλτον ἔχων χρυσέην τὰ Φιλοκράτεος δὲ Διαύλου
τραυλίζει ψυχῆς φίλτρα κατʼ Ἀντιγένους.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XII.163: εὗρεν Ἔρως τί καλῷ μίξει
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text:
εὗρεν Ἔρως τί καλῷ μίξει καλόν, οὐχὶ μάραγδον
χρυσῷ, ὃ μήτʼ ἀνθεῖ, μήτε γένοιτʼ ἐν ἴσῳ,
οὐδʼ ἐλέφαντʼ ἐβένῳ, λευκῷ μέλαν, ἀλλὰ Κλέανδρον
Εὐβιότῳ, πειθοῦς ἄνθεα καὶ φιλίης.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XII.166: τοῦθʼ ὅ τί μοι λοιπὸν
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text:
τοῦθʼ ὅ τί μοι λοιπὸν ψυχῆς, ὅ τι δή ποτʼ, Ἔρωτες,
τοῦτό γʼ ἔχειν πρὸς θεῶν ἡσυχίην ἄφετε·
ἢ μὴ δὴ τόξοις ἔτι βάλλετὲ μʼ, ἀλλὰ κεραυνοῖς·
ναὶ πάντως τέφρην θέσθε με κἀνθρακιήν.
ναί, ναί, βάλλετʼ, Ἔρωτες· ἐνεσκληκὼς γὰρ ἀνίαις,
ἐξ ὑμέων τοῦτʼ οὖν, εἴ γέ τι, βούλομʼ ἔχειν.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XIII.23: ἰὼ παρέρπων, μικρόν, εἴ τι
poems.author: Asclepiades of Samos
poems.text:
ἰὼ παρέρπων, μικρόν, εἴ τι κἀγκονεῖς, ἄκουσον
τὰ Βότρυος περισσὰ δῆτα κήδη,
ὃς πρέσβυς ὀγδώκοντʼ ἐτῶν τὸν ἐννέων ἔθαψεν
ἤδη τι τέχνᾳ καὶ σοφὸν λέγοντα.
φεῦ τὸν τεκόντα, φεῦ δὲ καὶ σέ, Βότρυος φίλος παῖ,
ὅσων ἄμοιρος ἡδονῶν ἀπώλευ.
